layer1.name: KilnBook
layer1.one_liner: Firing schedule booking for shared ceramics studios.
layer1.description: Kiln booking and firing-schedule management for shared studios. Halfway through discovery: every load-bearing assumption has real conversations behind it, none has enough to resolve.
layer1.outcome_note: Synthetic fixture. Not a real company and not counted toward separation statistics.

layer2.pins: The middle of the cap's range, which no other fixture occupies. Both assumptions sit at half their pre-registered sample size, so coverage is fractional, Evidence Quality lands near 50 and the cap near 65 — binding, but well above the floor. Also pins that partial coverage does not resolve a criterion: both assumptions stay untested and the confidence bands stay wide even though real conversations have happened.

assumptions.statement: At least 4 in 10 shared ceramics studios with 30 or more members have lost a firing slot to a double booking in the past year

falsification_criterion.applies_to: shared ceramics studios with 30 or more members
falsification_criterion.observation: ask the studio manager about their last kiln scheduling conflict
falsification_criterion.metric: count who lost a slot to a double booking

assumptions.statement: At least 3 in 10 shared ceramics studios contacted through regional craft guild lists reply within two weeks

falsification_criterion.applies_to: shared ceramics studios listed with regional craft guilds
falsification_criterion.observation: contact listed studios and count replies within two weeks

claims.text: A studio manager describes two members claiming the same firing slot last month.
A second manager keeps a paper sheet specifically to prevent double bookings.
A third studio has not had a conflict since capping member count.
A guild-listed studio replied within three days.
A second guild-listed studio replied within a week and booked a call.
A third listed studio did not reply within two weeks.
A regional craft guild publishes a filterable member studio directory.
